instruction: Make the title of the essay bold and center-aligned.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent selected all text (Ctrl+A) and used Format > Text > Capitalize Every Word to convert first letter of each word to uppercase. Completed in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select all text, navigate Format menu, apply text formatting in LibreOffice Writer
metadata.task_rationale: Original task applied formatting to all text; this variation tests selective formatting (bold + center) on just the title, requiring the model to select specific text and apply multiple formatting operations
metadata.explanation: Task requires making the first paragraph bold and center-aligned. Getter reads first paragraph formatting. Metric gives 0.5 for bold, 0.5 for centered (partial credit).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the first paragraph (title) of the docx file and checks both alignment (WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER) and bold status across all runs
Metric provides appropriate partial credit: 0.5 for bold, 0.5 for center-aligned, covering both instruction requirements
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring state freshness
Metric does not use the expected parameter (rules are empty {}), which is fine since all verification logic is self-contained in the getter result
Edge cases handled: no file, no paragraphs, no runs in paragraph
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: run.bold returns None when bold is inherited from paragraph style rather than explicitly set. If the title uses a style like 'Title' or 'Heading 1' that inherits bold, the check may not detect it. Consider also checking paragraph style font.bold as a fallback.
Minor: The assumption that paragraphs[0] is the title is reasonable for essays but could fail if there are empty paragraphs before the actual title.
